newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds overcame a spell of midday weakness to end higher, continuing a rally which has been largely intact since mid-January.
Swiss yields have fallen to lows unseen since 1979, leading to demand for longer-dated paper as investors try to counter a drop in 10-year yields to in some cases below 3.50 percent.

The Swiss Treasury, in a lightening action, sold 150 million of its outstanding 4-1/2 percent June 2007 bond, which was reopened in an auction January 23. The Treasury priced the issue at 108.65, about 10 basis points higher than where the issue traded at in the market when the offer was announced.
Traders said demand was heavy, noting that the Treasury's offer of 150 million francs was met with bids of 770 million.
"It went sensationally," said one dealer at a Zurich-based bank. "Demand was massive. In an offer which closed in 40 minutes, it was five times oversubscribed," the dealer added.

The market retraced some early gains after the Swiss government's tender, undermined by weakness in Bunds. But traders said that the Bund contract's ability to hold support at 102.75 helped to steady the Swiss market, generating fresh demand. Swiss bonds were most sought, while some traders said there was still an oversupply of foreign bonds.
New foreign issues launched since the start of February have thus far totaled roughly 1.5 billion Swiss francs.
March Conf futures CONFH7 up 13 at 120.53.
March Comi medium-term bond COMIH7 down five at 111.85
